title: Design a Forecasting Platform
interviewAnswer: A forecasting platform must ingest time-indexed data, define cutoffs/horizons, construct leakage-safe features, run rolling backtests, train/version models, generate probabilistic forecasts and monitor bias/accuracy by segment.
keyPoints: Backtest and production feature pipelines must match.
why: Design a Forecasting Platform appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: A forecasting platform must ingest time-indexed data, define cutoffs/horizons, construct leakage-safe features, run rolling backtests, train/version models, generate probabilistic forecasts and monitor bias/accuracy by segment. Backtest and production feature pipelines must match. Support fallback baselines. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Nightly demand forecasts for thousands of SKUs with holiday/weather drivers and reconciliation across product hierarchy.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Design a Forecasting Platform make?
How would you validate or debug Design a Forecasting Platform in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
